messages.subject: Water in the rear bathroom (2)
messages.body:
Ms. Raghunathan,

I have been informed by the cleaning service that there is again water on the floor of the rear bathroom. As I noted in my previous message (April 18), this is not a plumbing issue. The drainage system is functioning correctly.

What I am observing is:

1. Excessive water usage at the sinks
2. Paper towels disposed of improperly
3. Floor mats not being used as intended

I would ask that you remind your team to be mindful of water around the sink area. The floor seal in that bathroom is not rated for standing water.

Regards,
Ezra Mbeki-Toft
Premises Management

messages.subject: Water in the rear bathroom (2)
messages.body:
Ezra,

Just to make sure I understand: the floor is flooding because we are washing our hands too enthusiastically?

Best,
Priya

messages.subject: Water in the rear bathroom (2)
messages.body:
Ms. Raghunathan,

Not "flooding." Water accumulation due to usage patterns. The distinction is important from a liability perspective.

The sink basin is shallow and the faucet pressure is commercial-grade. When used without attention to splashing, water exits the basin perimeter and accumulates on the counter, then travels to the floor.

This is addressed in the Tenant Guidelines (section 4.2, "Proper Use of Facilities") which were provided at lease signing.

I can arrange for additional floor mats if that would help, though there will be a deposit required.

Regards,
Ezra Mbeki-Toft

messages.subject: Water in the rear bathroom (2)
messages.body:
We will be more careful. Thank you.

Best,
Priya
